knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")

```{r setup}
library(enrollcast)
```

## The grade progression ratio method

The cohort survival / grade progression ratio method projects enrollment by
asking: of the students in grade *g* this year, how many appear in grade *g+1*
next year? That ratio captures net retention, migration, and repetition.
`enrollcast` estimates these ratios from history and applies them forward with
a matrix projection.

## A small district

```{r}
history <- data.frame(
  year = rep(2021:2023, each = 3),
  grade = factor(rep(c("K", "1", "2"), 3), levels = c("K", "1", "2")),
  enrollment = c(100, 90, 80, 110, 95, 88, 120, 99, 91)
)
history
```

## Step 1: progression ratios

```{r}
ratios <- progression_ratios(history, method = "mean")
ratios
```

Ratios are calculated only from observed adjacent calendar-year pairs. If the
history contains a gap, `progression_ratios()` warns and uses the adjacent pairs
on either side without constructing a transition across the missing period. A
history with no adjacent year pair cannot produce progression ratios and is
rejected. Gap detection examines the complete supplied history before `n_years`
selects the most recent adjacent transitions, so an older gap still warns even
when it lies outside the selected transitions.

The ratios sit on the sub-diagonal of the projection matrix; the entry-grade row
is zero because entry is supplied exogenously.

```{r}
progression_matrix(ratios)
```

## Step 2: project forward

The entry grade (kindergarten here) has no feeder grade, so you supply its
future values — for example from a birth-cohort or housing model.

```{r}
base <- history[history$year == 2023, c("grade", "enrollment")]
projection <- project_enrollment(
  base = base,
  ratios = ratios,
  horizon = 3,
  entry = c(125, 130, 128),
  start_year = 2023
)
projection
```

## Stitching history and projection

`project_enrollment()` returns projected years only. Combine with history for
plotting:

```{r}
observed <- data.frame(
  year = history$year,
  grade = as.character(history$grade),
  enrollment = history$enrollment
)
combined <- rbind(observed, projection)
head(combined)
```

## Modeling a school modernization swing

A school temporarily relocated during modernization typically sees depressed
enrollment that recovers after it returns. `swing_schedule()` builds a per-year
projection schedule. Classes move up normally and a new entry class arrives
every year, including during swing and recovery. Each swing year's output is
rescaled to the base-year school total, and each recovery year's output is
rescaled to an explicit school target total.

```{r}
depressed <- c(K = 80, `1` = 66, `2` = 60)
schedule <- swing_schedule(ratios,
  horizon = 6, swing_years = 2,
  recovery = c(225, 245, 260), entry = rep(90, 6)
)
recovered <- project_enrollment(depressed, schedule = schedule, start_year = 2023)
recovered
tapply(recovered$enrollment, recovered$year, sum)
```

The first two annual totals equal `sum(depressed)` (206), followed by the
recovery targets 225, 245, and 260. In each of those years the projected
grades `n[h]` are rescaled to the target `T[h]` as `n[h] * T[h] / sum(n[h])`,
and the rescaled grades are the students who move up the next year. The entry
class is rescaled with the other grades, so reported entry enrollment in those
years is the supplied value times the year's adjustment, and a larger supplied
entry class gives a larger reported one.

After the last target year nothing is adjusted. The school continues from the
recovered grades using the progression ratios and the supplied `entry` values,
which are reported as given. Later totals therefore follow the ratios, and
drift toward the level the ratios and entry values sustain when the final
target is far from it. A school's own ratios can be inflated by recovery
growth; if so, supply ordinary ratios for the years after recovery through a
list for `ratios` (see below).

This replaces the former behavior that froze the grade mix during swing and
recovery. To migrate an earlier call, supply entry values for the entire
`horizon` and replace recovery multipliers with annual totals. For old
whole-school multipliers `multipliers`, the equivalent target path is
`sum(depressed) * cumprod(multipliers)`. Grade-specific recovery multiplier
matrices are no longer accepted.

### Changing ratios and opening grades

Supply a list of `horizon` ratios tables or projection matrices to vary ratios
by year. Matrices must share identical row and column grade names in the same
order, including grades that have yet to open. A zero destination row keeps a
grade closed; restore its progression ratio in the year it opens. An entry of
zero keeps the entry grade closed. Targets cover the whole school, so choose
them to fit the grades that are open in each year.

```{r}
m <- progression_matrix(ratios)
closed <- m
closed["2", ] <- 0
opening <- swing_schedule(
  ratios = list(closed, closed, m, m),
  horizon = 4, swing_years = 1,
  recovery = c(165, 235), entry = rep(90, 4)
)
project_enrollment(c(K = 80, `1` = 66, `2` = 0), schedule = opening)
```

### Schedule targets and missing values

A schedule step is `list(matrix = m, entry = value)`, with an optional `total`
that rescales that year's grades. `total = "base"` uses the sum of the aligned
base grades; a numeric `total` gives the target directly. The rescaled grades
feed the next step, and a step without a target applies no adjustment.
Hand-built identity or diagonal steps remain available through
`project_enrollment()`.

Schedules may contain `NA` or `NaN` matrix coefficients. These values are
preserved and warned about rather than imputed. A missing coefficient can make
its output grade missing. If that missing enrollment remains after entry
replacement, the next matrix multiplication spreads missingness to all grade
results because zero times a missing value is still missing. A non-`NULL` entry
value then restores only the entry grade.

To rescale, the projected school total must be finite and positive. A missing
or infinite total, or a positive target on a zero projection, raises an error.
When both the projection and target total are zero, the adjustment is one.
A zero target on a positive projection empties that year, cohorts included, so
only later entry classes remain for a later target to rescale.
